R5 — Final rendering pass

1

The animal followed shows through the grass

Was

A small animal in the local view vanished under the grass tufts drawn in front of it; only trees and bushes went see-through.

Now

Grass and the small things in front of the animal followed go see-through too, a little less than trees (40 % against 30 % opacity). Pebbles are left alone. By the owner's choice there is no minimum size.

Round 2, after the owner saw a tuft pop as an animal walked through it: "in front" is now judged by the same rows the animal is drawn in (its lowest point), not by the bottom of its box, so no tuft covers it whole any more; and plants ease to see-through and back over a quarter of a second instead of in one frame.

2

Colours straight from the genes

Was

Colour was each animal's own HUE at one saturation and lightness. Sister species differ by a few hundredths in every gene: in the creatures' recording eight of ten species have HUE between 0.92 and 0.97, so nearly every animal was red or magenta.

Now

Six genes set two colours (src/creatures/colours.ts), each read by its species' rank among the species alive, spread evenly over its range. The order is still the genes': the redder species stays further round the wheel. Each animal moves a little from its species by its own genes. Read again when a species appears or dies out, when every animal is redrawn.

Round 2 (the owner: "avoid olive"): body hues keep off the ground's yellow-greens (0.11–0.42 of the wheel), markings that fall there go to its nearer edge, and saturation starts at 0.5 instead of 0.32.

3

Round dots on the map

Was

Every animal was a square grown with its mass; the heaviest were big blocks.

Now

Round dots of whole pixels with a dark edge, in three sizes by mass, in the body's colour (src/creatures/markers.ts). Swimmers get a ring round a dark middle, and the young the smallest dot.

4

A calmer ground

Was

The middle view painted each cell's cover alone: a busy patchwork. In the local view, borders between kinds followed the blend's straight steps, and grass met bare soil with a hard edge while other borders were dithered.

Now

The middle view reads cover over the cells around each one, as the local view did, so it lies in patches. Borders wander with noise. Growth beside bare ground has a lip lit from the upper left: one pixel darker on its lower edge, one lighter on its upper.

5

Grass as a texture of small tufts

Was

Three drawings of one symmetric fan, three quarters of a cell across, a dark outline round every blade, one to four to a cell: each read as a shrub standing on the grass.

Now

Round 3, after references: grass in pixel art is a texture of small tufts, not things standing on it. A tuft is now about a third of a cell (12×8 art pixels), unoutlined: three to five spikes fanning out in a V from a narrow foot, darkest at the foot and brightest at the tips. Three shapes (a W, a fuller clump of two, spikes bent by the wind), each also mirrored; three to six to a cell by biomass, in clumps that cross cell borders, with gaps where the grass is thin.

Round 4, the owner: several sizes and some random change in colour. Nine drawings from 0.6 to 1.45 times the size, a large tuft growing wider (more spikes) rather than taller; each tuft takes one of five tints at random: none, warmer, cooler, darker, warmer and darker.

References: the grass of The Legend of Zelda: The Minish Cap as discussed in imonk, "Zelda style mockup, part 1: grass"; "Pixel tutorial: grass patches"; Slynyrd, Pixelblog 20: top-down tiles.

6

Snow only where the simulation has it

Was

The renderer kept a snow line of its own, so a bare summit wore a white cap in August among green grass.

Now

Bare heights are rock. Snow lies where the simulation puts it, by season and height. The fixed line stays only for a land without the simulation's snow (the R0 fixture).

7

The young

Was

Age was not on the wire: a newborn appeared at full size.

Now

creatures messages carry young: each young animal's id and how far grown it is, in sixteenths (from Population.maturity; additive, no schema bump). A newborn is drawn at half length with a head 35 % larger for its body, and is redrawn at each sixteenth until it comes of age. About 80 of the ~200 animals in the recording are young at any time.

·

Nothing stands on the water

Was

A plant was allowed by its cell's height, while the ground paints the coast between cells and the swash runs up the beach at high tide: near the shore a plant could stand in the sea (reeds most of all; since round 3 grass clumps spill into the next cell too).

Now

A plant's foot must be on the land as painted (heights between cells, as animals already read them) and as far from the waterline as the swash reaches in that view (10 art pixels up close). Its shadow goes with it.

·

Land animals in the water

Was

The simulation lets a land animal into the sea, where it pays for every hour and drowns when its energy runs out (M11 makes the shallow shelf free). The renderer drew it as if on land: walking on the water.

Now

The renderer shows the simulation's place, never moving an animal out, and draws the effort (the owner: struggling more than on land unless partly aquatic), 1 − AQUATIC / 0.6. In the shallows (no deeper than 0.03, M11's wading depth) its legs are under the water, it slows by up to 45 % and ripples spread from it. Out of its depth its legs are gone from sight, its body is sunk but for its head, it slows by up to 70 %, bobs, and the ripples come faster and wider (src/creatures/wading.ts).

·

Legs in turn, and no body folding through itself

Legs

A foot stepped when its rest point was far enough away, so a short-legged or slow body moved all its feet on the same frame. Now a legged body goes through a gait cycle for every 1.5 lengths of its shortest leg it walks. Each foot is in the air for 40 % of it and stands still for the rest. A pair's two feet are half a cycle apart and diagonal feet swing together: alternating with one pair, a trot with two, tripods with three. A foot never slides once down, and a body that stops brings its feet back under it.

Bodies

The chain followed the head with no limit, so a sharp turn folded it back over itself. Now each kind bends only so far from head to tail (worms and snakes into a U, beasts a little, beetles and crabs hardly), the head turns at most 0.6 rad from the body, long bodies walk a turn as an arc, short stiff ones turn on the spot, and looking about turns the head only. Over 10 simulated minutes per kind, joints folded onto each other in 16–26 % of frames before and none after.

·

Animals keep clear of trees and bushes

Was

Between the simulation's ticks an animal strolled anywhere that was land, so it walked through bushes and stood on trunks, and seemed to walk over the vegetation.

Now

Each tree and bush leaves a footprint (a tree's trunk and roots, a bush's lower puffs). Strolls pick clear goals and stop before a plant; the walk to where the simulation has the animal steers round them; a place the simulation puts inside a bush is drawn beside it, without changing the simulation's data. Grass and flowers are still walked through. In the middle view at (64, 64), 1–3 of about 14 animals were in a footprint at any moment before, and almost always none after.

Depth

Rounds 2–3 (the owner: parts of the creatures still seemed above the bushes). Top-down games sort by the base of each thing, which suits characters drawn from the side; ours are drawn from above, so one in front of a bush, or across it, seemed to lie on its leaves. Now the leaves of every tree and bush are over any animal they overlap, whichever side its feet are, and a bush's footprint is a band along its whole foot: animals go round a bush or behind it, never across its front.

Staged by hand round one bush (the owner: put the animals where they are to be seen rather than wait for them): three animals of three sizes sent from in front of it to behind it, from behind to in front, and past it sideways. The leaves are over any animal they overlap; a bush's foot is a band no animal stands across. The fade in front of the animal followed is off. Enlarged twice; there is no "before" (the scene before R5 has no hooks to stage it).

Five animals of different sizes followed among bushes, 12 s each, the middle of the screen enlarged twice: before left, after right.

·

Bushes in pieces

Why

The owner, still unsatisfied with animals among bushes: perhaps draw the bushes in pieces. Tried beside the whole bushes and chosen by the owner on 2026-10-24: the pieces are now the default (?bushes=whole draws them whole), with no fade in front of the animal followed.

How

Each puff of a bush in the local view is a sprite of its own, cut from the same drawing (each pixel to the puff painted last over it), so a bush with no animal near looks as before. Each piece is sorted by the foot of its puff and keeps a small footprint of its own (0.85 of its radius across, 0.5 deep): together they block the lower two-thirds of the bush, so animals pass behind its top puffs and between bushes. A piece is over an animal only where a joint of the animal is behind its foot and under its drawing: in front of a puff an animal is drawn over it, between puffs it is behind the back ones and under the front ones. Trees, sprouts and fire pines stay whole. In the wind each piece slides by whole art pixels as far as the whole drawing would lean at its height, all the pieces of a bush with the same gust (src/plants/pieces.ts, PlantLayer.blow).

The staged walks in the section above are drawn with the bushes in pieces; the storm film in the wind section shows them leaning.

·

The name card of the animal followed

The owner's choice

While the local view follows an animal: its species' name, its traits in words where words do well, pixel icons where they don't, always on, in a corner of the screen. The phone's follow-a-creature (S3) shows the same card.

Now

A field-guide card, top-left (the chronicle's scroll unrolls at the foot): cream in a thin wooden frame, the species' name on a sage heading band, a portrait of the animal itself on a plate, drawn from its genes in its own colours by the scene's creature layer, posed straight and facing right; beside it at most three words, one to a ruled line, for size (by mass: small, mid-sized, large), build (armoured, finned, swift, sluggish, legless, two-, six-, eight-legged, long- or short-legged) and diet (grazer, omnivore, hunter: the sim's own classes); under them icons for water-loving and each rare gene (fangs, warning sign, up arrow for giant, hourglass, frog, snowflake, leaf, sparkle for glow). It slides in when the camera settles on the animal and out when it leaves or visits an entry's place (src/card.ts, src/creatures/portrait.ts, window.__card()).

Cropped from the films above, the top-left corner at the art pixels' size. The recordings have few rare-gene carriers, so few icons show here.

21

The chronicle's scroll, illuminated

The owner's choice

The two scrolls different, both better: the chronicle stays parchment (it is the island's history) but illuminated; the name card becomes a field-guide card (above).

Now

An icon for the kind of event (a seedling for a new species, a skull for an extinction, a crown for a record, a flame, a volcano, a boat for newcomers, a heart for a boom, an arrow down for a crash…), an initial two lines tall in the species' own colour (vermilion when it names none), the date on a red ribbon pinned across the top, a larger hand in balanced lines, the scroll as wide as its text. Lit like a lantern at night. (src/illumination.ts, HAND_FONT.)

22

Eating

Was

Animals walked, rested and looked about; nothing showed what they do. Half of them are grazing at any moment.

Now

The stream says who is grazing (plants or algae) and who is feeding on meat. One that eats stands where it is: a grazer reaches to the ground in nibbles, three and a pause to chew, a flake of green at its mouth; one on meat tugs side to side and back, flecks of red. Staged here on open grass, enlarged twice: the large lizard grazing, the animal on the right feeding on meat.

·

Hunting and births

Was

A kill was a scuffle where the prey stood, with no hunter near; a newborn faded in wherever the simulation put it.

Now

The sim tells who killed each prey and whose each newborn is (died[].by, born[].parent on the wire; outputs only). A hunter that still lives runs to its prey round trees and bushes, at least 2.5 times its walking pace for 0.4–1.2 s, stops half its length short, and springs, its head thrust at the prey, dust from its hind feet; at the strike the prey dies as a kill does. A newborn appears beside its mother's head, facing her, clear of trees and bushes; she stands over it 2.6 s and lowers her head to it twice while three pixel hearts rise. A mother of broods of three or more lays: the young is an egg that rocks, cracks and comes apart (src/creatures/hunting.ts, nursery.ts). Staged on open grass, enlarged twice.

·

Rare genes in action

Why

Rare genes were only marks on the body (fangs, leaves, gills); the owner asked to see them at work. Only drawn: nothing new on the wire, the sim unchanged.

How

A photosynthesiser (leaves) standing about in daylight on dry land, not eating, asleep or busy, settles after 1.2 s and spreads out flat to the sun over 1.4 s: body 40 % wider and its parts further out, pressed lower, legs straight out to the sides; a star of sunlight glints on its back every 1.2–2.8 s. It gets up in a third of a second when it moves on, at dusk, or under cloud or rain (src/creatures/basking.ts). A venomous hunter's hunt is as any other's but for the strike: a lime star at the bite, two drips falling from it, every other puff of the prey's scuffle green, and green wisps rising as the dust settles (venom.ts, remains.ts). A swimmer, or an amphibian (gills) in the water, leaves a V of foam while it moves: every 4 art pixels a pair of 3-pixel dashes beside it at its widest, laid along the V's arms, drifting out, shortening and fading over 1.5 s; none standing still (wake.ts). All are marks of whole art pixels (sparks.ts). Staged by hand on the large lizard, each gene granted with window.__grant; enlarged twice.

·

Family life

Why

The owner (2026-10-24): the young should trail their mothers until grown, and a pair nuzzle briefly before a birth. Drawn only: the sim has no families beyond who bore whom (born[].parent), and nothing on the wire changes.

How

The scene remembers the mother of each young animal it sees born (a page loaded mid-life has no pairs until the next births) and forgets her when the young one comes of age (young on the wire) or either dies. While the sim has the two within 3 cells, the young one makes for a spot behind her tail and a little to one side, walking after her as she goes and trotting (1.4 times its pace) when more than 1.2 of its lengths behind; the spot is kept within 0.85 of its leash of where the sim has it, so it is never drawn off its own place. The young of one mother go in a line, each behind the one born before it. At a birth, the grown one of her kind nearest her head (within 2.2 cells and 2.5 s of a trot) comes up to the side of her head away from where her young will lie; their heads lean together for 1.4 s while two hearts rise, then the young are born as before (src/creatures/family.ts, motion.ts). Staged on open grass, enlarged twice.

·

Sleep at night

Now

Only drawn: the sim does not sleep. As the light goes each animal lies down at its own moment (from its genome), curled as far as its body bends, feet tucked, eyes shut to a slit, breathing slower and deeper; it wakes over the dawn. Animals with glow, keen senses (SENSE ≥ 0.8) and swimmers stay up. Moved far by the sim, or reached by the water, it gets up and walks, and settles again a few seconds later. A small "z" rises over the animal followed (src/creatures/sleep.ts).

·

Small life about the island

Now

Decoration only, on a random stream of its own, from pooled sprites: fireflies blinking over grass and shrub at night (middle and local views); a V of one to four gulls crossing the middle view by day, with a faint shadow; three butterflies over the meadows in the local view in spring and summer; puffs of dust from the hind feet of an animal hurrying on dry land. Nothing in rain, on the map or during a world's end (src/atmosphere/ambient.ts).

·

Plants in the wind

Now

Grass, flowers, ferns, reeds, bushes and the crowns of trees lean with the wind by whole art pixels, drawn again leaning one pixel back and up to three with it: rows slide, none below a hinge, a crown as one piece, so nothing smears and trunks stay put. Gusts of value noise roll east-south-east at 2.2 cells a second, so neighbours move together. It blows harder in rain and much harder in a thunderstorm, softer at night; ?still keeps every plant straight (src/plants/wind.ts, PlantLayer.blow). Enlarged twice.

·

Autumn leaves, and animals in the rain

Now

Drawn only. In autumn a few leaves come loose from the crowns of broadleaves shown in autumn (not those evergreen enough to keep their leaves, no conifers), in the colour each tree has turned, and fall with the plants' wind, swinging and flipping, to lie a moment by the tree and go: more late in autumn, in gusts, in rain and most in a thunderstorm; a tree drops one every ten seconds or so on a calm day. Whole art pixels (a pixel in the middle view, a small leaf in the plants' two-pixel texels up close), pooled, sorted among the plants; none on the map (src/atmosphere/leaves.ts, PlantLayer.crownAt). When a rain spell ends, each animal that was out in it stops and shakes once, a shiver down its body from head to tail and a spray of drops either side, at its own moment within four seconds; in a thunderstorm animals hunch, lower, feet drawn in, heads back, in shorter, slower steps. Swimmers, the torpid, sleepers and animals in deep water are left alone (src/creatures/weather.ts). Staged with ?season=autumn:0.9 and __rain("none").

8·9

Deaths by cause, bones, and landings from the sea

Was

Every death was the same fade where the animal last stood (but for the fire's ash), and animals that landed from the sea faded in like births.

Now

The sim tells who died of what (CreaturesDied, an output only: no saved state changes) and the wire carries died and landed on the creatures message. The body stops, turns toward its cause's colour, and comes apart in steps, legs first, tail to head (no see-through filter any more). The starved lie still and pale; the old the same, slower; a kill goes under a scuffle of dust; the drowned sink blue with bubbles and rings; the burnt char under R4's ash; a blast takes them at once. Pixel bones lie where the body lay, charred for the burnt, none for the drowned or the blasted, as the sim leaves carrion; they stay half a sim-day and fade over the other half. An animal that lands from the sea is there at once under a splash of drops and rings, in a wet patch that dries (src/creatures/remains.ts).

Each film is a fixed view on where the animal was last seen, enlarged twice; deaths come in the stream's creatures messages, every two sim-hours. No landing from the sea happens in the committed recordings (no founders, strangers or ark in them); the splash was checked on a staged ark stream.
